The Phoenix Mills LimitedAt The Phoenix Mills Limited, growth is guided by 
purpose and built on intent. As India’s leading retail-
led mixed-use developer, we capitalize on scale as 
a powerful lever for long-term value creation. With 
a presence across the country’s key consumption 
hubs, we unlock synergies by combining institutional 
expertise with local insight. By integrating retail 
with modern day anchors like offices and hotels 
or residential, we combine the power of scale with 
structural strength—reinforcing our leadership and 
enhancing the performance of every destination.Scale, however, delivers its full potential only when paired with 
agility. In a fast-evolving landscape, our ability to act with speed, 
precision, and discipline drives results. We adopt a granular, 
insight-driven approach to asset performance; curating dynamic 
tenant experiences, optimizing layouts, and responding to shifts 
in consumer behaviour with clarity and control. This culture of 
operational agility allows us to enhance yields, protect margins, 
and consistently outperform in a rapidly evolving environment. This 
discipline extends to our financial management: as of FY2025, 
net debt/EBITDA stood at 1.2x, gross debt at ` 4,409 crore (below 
FY2019 levels), and cost of debt reduced to 8.5%, all achieved 
through a prudent use of cash flows.
Even as we lead in the present, we remain firmly focused on 
building tomorrow by investing in landmark developments and 
sustainable practices that will shape the future of urban living. Our 
long-term roadmap is a testament to this commitment: we are 
advancing to expand our retail portfolio from 11.5 million sq. ft. to 
over 18 million sq. ft. by 2030, with a clear trajectory already in 
motion. Anchored by this vision, we continue to deliver iconic retail 
destinations integrated with immersive workspaces and hospitality 
experiences that celebrate global cultures and craftsmanship. We 
embed environmental stewardship and community engagement 
into every phase of each development, ensuring our assets endure 
as vibrant centres of economic and social interaction.
• Capitalising on Scale means 
thinking beyond footprint—it’s 
about creating ecosystems greater 
than the sum of their parts. 
• Enhancing Yield through 
Agility means cultivating a  
culture of continuous 
improvement, managing every 
asset with intelligence and 
discipline, anticipating change, 
adapting swiftly, and turning 
insight into lasting value. 
• Building Tomorrow means 
envisioning what cities need 
next—and delivering it with 
purpose, foresight, and 
responsibility.Together, scale, agility, and foresight define  
our strategic philosophy. At PML, growth is 
never incidental - it is scale applied with 
purpose, assets managed with discipline, 
and futures built with vision.

INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25
INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25
About this  
Report
This Integrated Annual Report presents a comprehensive account of The Phoenix Mills Limited’s (PML) 
performance, strategy, and outlook for the year ended March 31, 2025. It reflects our continued commitment to 
transparent communication and stakeholder engagement, offering a holistic view of both our financial and non-
financial performance.
The Report has been prepared in accordance with 
the International Integrated Reporting Framework 
(IIRC) and incorporates disclosures in line with 
the Companies Act, 2013, applicable rules, 
Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, and relevant Secretarial 
Standards. To strengthen comparability and 
global alignment, the Report integrates references 
to the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards 
and maps our contributions to the United Nations 
Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDGs).
The reporting boundary includes PML on both a 
standalone and consolidated basis, covering key 
business segments: retail, commercial offices, 
hospitality and residential projects. It spans the 
period from April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025, 
while also including forward-looking insights 
relevant to our long-term strategy.
The intended readership includes our 
shareholders and investors, tenants and brand 
partners, customers, regulators, employees,  
and communities, along with the broader 
ecosystem of stakeholders engaged with  
PML ’s growth journey.
For any queries or feedback, stakeholders may 
write to investorrelations@phoenixmills.com.How to Read this Report
This Integrated Annual Report is designed to provide 
a clear and connected understanding of PML ’s 
performance, strategy, and value creation. To enhance 
navigation and maximise reader engagement, the 
report uses a structured approach supported by 
icons, cross-references, and visual elements.
Key features to guide your reading:
1. Icons and Visual Aids: These symbols highlight 
our strategic pillars, material issues, and 
elements of the business model, enabling 
readers to connect themes across  
chapters quickly.
2. Material Issue Numbers: These references link 
critical ESG and business issues to relevant 
sections of the report.
3. Strategic Pillars: Our nine strategic pillars  
act as the backbone of our long-term vision. 
Look for these icons to understand how each 
initiative ties into our overarching growth agenda.
4. Business Model Elements: Based on the 
Business Model Canvas framework, these icons 
illustrate how our activities, resources, and 
partnerships combine to create and sustain value.
5. UNSDG Mapping: The alignment of our business 
activities with global goals is denoted by UNSDG 
icons, reflecting our contribution to sustainable 
urbanisation.
6. GRI References: References to GRI standards 
offer readers an easy pathway to assess 
our adherence to international reporting 
benchmarks.Navigating the Report:
Begin with the letters from the Chairman and the 
Managing Director, which provide an overview of PML ’s 
vision and performance during FY2025. Each capital 
chapter provides a deep dive into financial and non-
financial performance, supported by case studies, KPIs, 
and cross-references to related sections. The Strategic 
Pillars chapter explains our long-term roadmap, while 
the Business Model and Market Context chapters set 
out the foundation of how we create and sustain value. 
The report closes with statutory disclosures, governance 
reports, and financial statements to provide a complete 
picture of the Company.
By following these navigation cues, readers 
can gain both a high-level perspective 
and a detailed understanding of PML’s 
performance and future direction.

The Phoenix Mills Limited www.thephoenixmills.comAt Phoenix, we build destinations that people love 
to visit and return to, places that become the heart 
of their cities. This year’s theme, “ Capitalizing on 
Scale | Enhancing Yield through Agility | Building 
Tomorrow”  reflects both our operating performance 
and our long-term vision. As India continues to 
urbanize, this theme matters now more than ever.
For us, scale has always been about building 
ecosystems that endure. As cities grow and 
evolve, the demand for trusted, well-designed, and 
integrated destinations has never been greater. By 
enhancing yields at our operating assets through 
agility and discipline, we strengthen resilience in a 
dynamic environment. And in building tomorrow, we 
remain focused on turning ambition into reality.
FY2025 was a year of strong delivery across PML: 
consumption in our malls touched new highs, our 
offices and hotels scaled up, and our balance 
sheet remained resilient. At the same time, we 
laid the foundations for what PML will look like in 
2030: a portfolio that is larger yet diversified, more 
integrated, and designed to endure. Reflecting on FY2025
FY2025 was a year of broad-based strength across 
our portfolio. 
Retail: Our retail portfolio delivered all-time-high 
consumption of ` 13,750 crore, up 21% year-on-
year and rental income growth kept pace with 
consumption. This performance was led by strong 
contributions from new destinations such as 
Phoenix Mall of Asia in Bengaluru, Phoenix Mall 
of the Millennium in Pune, Palladium Ahmedabad, 
and Phoenix Citadel in Indore. Further, established 
centres like Phoenix Palladium (Mumbai), Phoenix 
Palassio (Lucknow), and our Phoenix MarketCity 
malls also continued to grow. Overall, this 
demonstrates the enduring strength of India’s 
urban consumption, and that well-curated retail 
destinations remain the preferred choice for both 
consumers and brands alike.
Looking ahead, we have initiated repositioning 
and premiumisation initiatives at our Phoenix 
MarketCity centres that will unlock significant

maintained healthy liquidity position. We continued 
to invest in growth, including acquisition of new 
land parcels in 3 cities and securing additional 
development potential at Lower Parel, alongside 
funding ongoing project spends. We closed the 
year with a conservative leverage position of ~1.2x 
Net Debt to EBITDA. Finally, we reinforced our 
commitment to shareholder value by announcing a 
`2.50 per share dividend. 
The letter from our Group Managing Director, 
Shishir, offers a detailed view of our financials and 
asset-level performance.Our Vision & 2030 Pipeline
Our journey ahead is about scaling with purpose: 
deepening our presence in established markets 
through densification of our landmark destinations, 
while expanding into new cities and  
integrated formats. 
Our existing destinations continue to attract the 
best of global and domestic brands, support 
strong consumption growth, and offer ample 
headroom for further expansion. At several of our 
assets, we have additional development potential 
that will be utilized to expand existing retail, and 
adding new offices and/or luxury hotels, ensuring 
that each location evolves into a more integrated 
urban ecosystem. 
Complete transformation of our ever-evolving 
complex in Lower Parel, Mumbai.  
What began with High Street Phoenix in the late 
1990s evolved into Mumbai’s first true luxury retail 
destination, Phoenix Palladium. The integration 
of a luxury hotel in 2012, rebranded as The St. 
Regis Mumbai in 2015, demonstrated the positive impact of hospitality within a mixed-use ecosystem, 
attracting global brands, marquee events, and 
discerning consumers. Over the last decade, 
EBITDA has grown nearly 4x from ` 168 crore in 
FY2013 to ` 648 crore in FY2025. 
Looking ahead, we are further densifying the Lower 
Parel development. Construction is underway 
offices and retail expansion, targeted for completion 
by 2027, with an additional 1.5 msft of development 
potential currently under design and approvals. In 
total, we have secured more than 3 msft of new 
potential since 2021. These additions will complete 
Lower Parel’s transformation into a fully integrated 
urban ecosystem, sustaining its strong EBITDA 
trajectory and reinforcing its position as one of 
Mumbai’s most iconic destinations.

From the established Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore,

integrated campus anchored by destination retail 
and elevated by new developments. The expansion 
of the retail at this asset through Gourmet Village,

A Defining Milestone: Buyout of 
CPP Investments’ 49% stake in 
ISMDPL
In July 2025, we announced one of the defining 
steps in our journey: the consolidation of CPP 
Investments’ 49% stake in Island Star Mall 
Developers Private Limited (ISMDPL). With this 
transaction, PML will have full ownership and control 
of irreplaceable destination assets including Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore, Phoenix Mall of Asia in 
Bengaluru, Phoenix Mall of the Millennium in 
Pune, and Phoenix Citadel Indore.
The significance of this deal goes beyond 
ownership. It enables us to consolidate the 
growing cash flows of ISMDPL, retain flexibility 
for future fund-raising, and preserve optionality 
for monetization, whether through a public listing 
or selective asset-level platforms, at a time of our 
choosing.
Importantly, the transaction has been structured 
to be largely self-funded at the ISMDPL level, 
with payouts staggered over four tranches. This 
ensures minimal strain on group liquidity and 
reflects our philosophy of capital-efficient growth.
This milestone reaffirms our confidence in the 
enduring quality of our portfolio. We remain 
grateful to CPP Investments for their valued 
partnership over the years, and look forward to 
continuing our collaboration through our other 
joint venture projects, including Project Rise in 
Mumbai and Phoenix Grand Victoria in Kolkata.
People & Culture
Our progress would not be possible without our 
people. As PML grows in scale and complexity, 
What excites me most is the depth of leadership 
we are building and also the values that anchor 
us: agility, integrity, and collaboration. These are 
the qualities that will carry Phoenix into its  
next decade.
This year, I am especially proud to see two 
colleagues, who have been at the heart of our 
journey, take on larger leadership roles. Rashmi 
Sen, a driving force behind our retail business 
for 14 years, was elevated as CEO – Malls. Her 
ability to balance retailer relationships, consumer 
insights, and strategic priorities has made our 
retail malls the preferred destinations for brands 
and consumers alike. Rajesh Kulkarni, who has 
shaped our design and delivery ethos for 18 
years, was elevated to CEO – Projects Delivery 
& Architecture. His calm yet creative leadership 
has been instrumental in building iconic 
destinations across India on time and  
within budgets.
Alongside these elevations, we also welcomed 
fresh leadership in areas critical to our future 
portfolio. Vithal Suryavanshi joined as CEO – Commercial Real Estate and Varun Chhibber as CEO 
– Hotels, strengthening businesses that will play a 
central role in our growth over the next decade.
We are committed to investing in learning, wellbeing, 
and inclusion across all levels, ensuring meaningful 
career pathways for our people. The combination of 
long-serving leaders who embody our values and 
fresh talent that brings new perspectives gives me 
confidence that we will continue to execute with 
excellence. Human capital remains our greatest 
strength: the foundation of today’s delivery and the 
engine of tomorrow’s growth.
Our Commitment to Sustainability 
& Society
Our approach to sustainability is grounded in 
responsibility and efficiency. Across our portfolio, 
we continue to adopt energy-efficient practices, 
water conservation initiatives, and advanced waste 
management systems; measures that reduce our 
footprint while enhancing operational efficiency. We 
are also expanding our pipeline of certified green 
buildings and steadily transitioning to renewable 
energy sources.
Our responsibility extends beyond the environment 
to the communities we serve. Through our 
partnership with the Aakar Charitable Trust, we 
supported the construction of dams and ponds 
across Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Gujarat; 
strengthening water security and agricultural 
productivity for ~192 villages, during FY2025. 
Alongside this, we continue to support initiatives in 
education, rural upliftment, and social welfare.
Closing
FY2025 has been a year of both delivery and 
preparation and a proof of what we can achieve 
today, with a clear signal of the scale we are 
building for tomorrow. As we look ahead, we remain 
committed to creating destinations that define 
urban life in India, and doing so with responsibility, 
discipline, and a value-driven culture.

The Phoenix Mills LimitedFollowing an exceptionally strong FY2024, this 
year represented a year of steady performance 
and strategic progress across our portfolio. 
Consolidated revenue from operations stood at 
`3,814 crore and consolidated EBITDA remained 
robust at `2,161 crore.
FY2025 was a year where intent translated into 
delivery, underscoring PML ’s discipline, cash-flow 
strength, and long-term value creation. Our theme 
this year: “ Capitalising on Scale | Enhancing 
Yield through Agility | Building Tomorrow” , is 
reflected in our performance. We capitalised on 
scale by leveraging our pan-India retail portfolio 
to deliver strong operational performance. We 
advanced towards enhancing yields through 
agility, by maintaining financial discipline and by 
initiating an asset repositioning exercise across key 
MarketCity malls, to drive higher productivity in the 
years ahead. And we continued building tomorrow, 
advancing our pipeline across retail, offices, hotels, 
and residences to shape the portfolio that will  
define 2030.
Following an exceptionally strong FY2024, this 
year represented a year of steady performance 
and strategic progress across our portfolio. 
Consolidated revenue from operations stood at 
`3,814 crore and consolidated EBITDA remained 
robust at ` 2,161 crore.Our core businesses i.e. retail, offices, and hotels 
were the key drivers, with revenue from these 
segments rising by 16% to ` 3,507 crore, while 
EBITDA also grew 16% to ` 2,111 crore. This 
performance reflects the scale and quality of our 
assets, and the operational discipline that enables 
us to deliver consistent growth. Looking ahead, 
these results position us strongly to capture 
opportunities across cycles and create long-term 
value for all stakeholders.
Retail: Shaping the Future of 
Consumption Hubs
Retail has always been at the core of PML ’s growth 
story, beginning with the pioneering High Street 
Phoenix in the 1990s, expanding through our 
Phoenix MarketCity portfolio with four malls launched 
between 2011 and 2013, and further strengthened 
by 5 new launches from 2020 to 2023. Today, with 
11.5 million sq. ft. of operational space across 12 
malls in 8 cities, we continue to set new benchmarks 
in scale, quality, and customer experience.

INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25FY2025 was a milestone year for our retail business. 
Consumption reached a record ` 13,750 crore, 
up 21% year-on-year, and an 18% rise in rental 
income to ` 1,951 crore and a 20% increase in 
asset EBITDA to ` 2,010 crore. Leased occupancy 
in the retail portfolio was strong at over 95%, 
demonstrating stability of our established malls and 
the momentum of new assets.
A highlight was the launch of West Zone at Phoenix 
Palladium, Mumbai, where we added ~250,000 
sq. ft. and brought marquee brands such as 
Uniqlo’s largest South Mumbai store and the India 
debut of Bershka, to name a few.  The West Zone 
also houses Gourmet Village, a two-level dining 
and entertainment hub, including Game Palacio 
(launched in July 2025) and other leisure formats 
such as pickle ball and paddle courts (which are 
currently under development). These additions are 
transforming Phoenix Palladium into a destination 
blending retail, dining, and lifestyle.
Momentum across the wider portfolio was equally 
strong with Palladium Ahmedabad, Phoenix Mall 
of the Millennium in Pune and Phoenix Mall of Asia 
in Bengaluru recording sharp gains in occupancy. 
Collectively, during FY2025 our malls welcomed 
over 130 million visitors and added over 350 stores, 
underscoring resilient demand.
In parallel, we initiated a repositioning strategy across 
our Phoenix MarketCity in Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, 
and Bengaluru which includes curating premium 
brands, rationalising under-performing stores, and 
enhancing layouts. At the same time, we continue to 
leverage data-driven insights to personalise customer 
experiences and enhance tenant productivity. These 
steps strengthen consumption today while laying 
the foundation for sustained growth and higher 
productivity over the long term.
Offices: Modern Anchors to 
Integrated Destinations
The natural evolution of our retail-led model is the 
creation of integrated ecosystems that encompass 
work, leisure, and living. 
Our office strategy rests on three enduring pillars: 
People, Product, and Proximity. With experienced 
project teams delivering Grade-A workspaces, and 
leasing teams with a deep regional focus, we are 
confident of sustaining strong occupancies and 
tenant curation in the future. Strategically located and designed with premium amenities, embedded 
sustainability features, and independent access and 
security, our offices meet global standards while 
being tailored to their cities. What sets them apart 
is their integration within our retail destinations, 
providing occupiers unparalleled access to dining, 
wellness, and culture, creating workplaces  
of choice.
In FY2025, our operating office portfolio (comprising 
offices in Mumbai and at Vimannagar in Pune) 
generated `210 crore in income up 10%, with 
EBITDA rising 19% to ` 131 crore and occupancy  
of ~67%. New offices in Bengaluru, Pune and Chennai are 
steadily building leasing momentum, backed by 
our three pillars. At One National Park, Chennai, 
leasing demand has been particularly robust, with 
nearly 50% pre-leased (as of July 2025), ahead of 
Occupation Certificate (OC): a clear validation of 
the strength of our office product and strategy. In 
this calendar year, we are seeing very good interest 
at Phoenix Asia Towers (Bengaluru) and Millennium 
Towers (Pune).
By layering modern day anchors such as offices 
onto our retail base, we diversify income streams 
and further strengthen the prominence of  
our destinations.
Hospitality: Expanding Luxury and 
Lifestyle Experiences
Our hospitality portfolio complements our retail and 
office assets, transforming destinations into vibrant 
lifestyle hubs.  In FY2025, the portfolio delivered 
revenue of ` 580 crore, up 6% year-on-year, with 
EBITDA rising 11% to ` 266 crore and margins 
improving to 46%. 
During FY25, The St. Regis, Mumbai, saw income 
of `523 crore, up 7% YoY, driven by higher RevPAR 
and ARR, and occupancy of 86%. EBITDA for the year at The St. Regis, Mumbai, stood at ` 248 crore 
with a margin of 47%, reaffirming its leadership as 
South Mumbai’s premier luxury destination.
Courtyard by Marriott, Agra, delivered steady 
growth, with revenue up 4% to ` 57 crore and 
EBITDA at ` 18 crore, benefiting from resilient 
domestic leisure demand.
Residential: Creating Lasting Value 
in Luxury Living
Our residential projects are envisioned as addresses 
of distinction, blending architectural excellence with 
thoughtful community design.
During the year, our projects delivered steady 
performance. Kessaku and One Bangalore West 
(Towers 1–7) in Bengaluru, recorded gross sales 
of `212 crore and collections of ` 219 crore. Our 
residential portfolio continues to demonstrate strong 
capital appreciation: average selling prices rose  
to `26,000 per sq. ft. in FY2025, a 63% jump  
since FY2020.

our office portfolio.
Looking ahead, the next few years will be about

At The Phoenix Mills Limited (PML) our retail legacy spans over two decades. Yet 
from the very beginning, our ambition extended beyond retail. We aspired to build 
vibrant urban destinations, where daily life – working, shopping, dining, living and 
leisure come together in a seamless, sustainable way. That vision is now a tangible 
reality. Across India’s top cities, our assets have evolved into high-density, integrated 
mixed-use developments. These are not just buildings; they are thriving ecosystems 
designed for sustained engagement and long-term value creation.The Mixed-Use Edge
Designing for Density,  
Delivering for the Future
Designing with Intention
The strength of our model lies in the way every 
component of our assets enhances the others. Our 
model is built on the insight that when one person 
can engage across multiple touchpoints (work, retail, 
dining, hospitality, and residence), they stay longer, 
return more often, and create more value per visit.
But we don’t apply this model everywhere. We 
build mixed-use ecosystems only where conditions 
allow for sustained, high-value performance. Each 
site is evaluated for its “right to win”—based on its 
location, socio-economic drivers, evolving urban 
needs,and regulatory potential. This strategic 
selectivity ensurescapital is deployed where it  
can compound.We also build with optionality. In emerging markets 
like Lucknow and Ahmedabad, we have launched 
with a retail destination mall as the first phase—
while retaining the flexibility to add complimentary 
asset classes including offices and hotels as local 
ecosystems mature.
Intentional design builds synergy. 
Optionality ensures relevance over time.

Phoenix MarketCity Banglore: Making of an Icon
Launched in 2011 with ~1 million sq. ft. of retail, Phoenix MarketCity 
Bangalore is a living model of mixed-use densification. By 2030, it is set to 
evolve into a 4 million+ sq. ft. integrated development —combining retail, 
commercial offices, and hospitality into a single high-performance  
urban destination.
Ongoing Transformation*:
 Retail: Expansion from ~1 million sq. ft to ~1.8 million sq. ft.
 y~0.17 million sq. ft. to be added by 2026 
 y~0.60 million sq. ft. expansion under planning
 Offices: Expanding to ~1.6 million sq. ft. by 2030
 y~0.4 million sq. ft. of office space by 2027; 
 y~1.20 million sq. ft. addition under planning
 Hospitality: Adding two hotels by 2030
 yGrand Hyatt upto 400 keys, by 2027
 yA second 300-key hotel under planning
Why Scale Matters:
Larger retail formats not only enhance variety but also extend dwell time 
and drive consumption. With scale, Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore can:
 Attract broader catchment areas and become an all-day destination
 Enable flagship store formats and richer lifestyle experiences; including 
dining, entertainment, and leisure
 Boost footfall, increase average spend, and improve trading densityThe Mixed-Use Advantage:
By layering in offices and hotels, with 
retail, the campus becomes a vibrant 24/7 
destination, creating deeper engagement. 
Together, these components:
 Anchor weekday traffic driven by 
office tenants and business travelers
 Enhance monetization by extending 
peak activity beyond weekends
 Drive higher asset productivity and 
improved tenant retention through 
continuous engagement
Together, scale and integration lead to 
higher consumption, drive higher rentals 
and stronger yields, ultimately creating 
long-term asset value.

Phoenix MarketCity 
Bangalore into a 
highperformance urban 
campus— where scale 
and integration unlock 
sustained growth.
Commercial Offices: 
Embedding Work-Life 
Synergy
In today’s experience-driven world, 
offices must offer more than functional 
space, they must be part of an 
integrated ecosystem. Our commercial 
developments are designed to meet 
evolving tenant expectations by 
combining efficiency with lifestyle-
focused amenities.
Each property features a distinct arrival

Inside, thoughtfully designed amenity

Tenants also benefit from seamless

- shopping, dining, entertainment, 
and hospitality, enhancing everyday 
convenience. Proximity to urban transit 
simplifies commutes and broadens talent 
reach. Together, these elements elevate 
tenant satisfaction, improve retention, 
and position our offices as aspirational 
places to work.
In FY2025, our operational offices 
generated income of `210 crore, with 
EBITDA rising 19% to `131 crore. New 
assets like Phoenix Asia Towers in

Towers in Pune received Occupation

wellness-oriented workspaces to 
our portfolio. As of March 2025, we 
had over 1.2 million square feet in 
active pre-leasing discussions across 
Bengaluru, Pune, and Chennai.
Offices today must do more than  
house teams—they must support 
the lives around them. Mixed-
use makes that possible.
Hotels: Performance Engines for Urban 
Ecosystems
Our hotels do more than serve guests, they elevate every surrounding 
asset. They support weekday office density, stimulate retail and F&B 
activity, and attract event-based business tourism. Whether hosting 
investor summits or luxury weddings, our hospitality assets extend stay 
duration, enrich experience, and enhance monetization across the board.
FY2025 marked a new high in our hospitality vertical, with The St. Regis 
Mumbai recording `523 crore in revenue, 86% occupancy, 15% growth 
in RevPAR and 11% rise in ADRs.
Our hotels activate traffic, extend dwell time, and 
create meaningful use cases for every square foot.

Why It Works: A model that delivers sustained

Each component, retail, offices, hotels, are not simply co-located, but intentionally

key urban centres, our integrated model has consistently delivered strong, sustained 
financial performance.
This multi-layered model activates every square

Our Business Model: Integrated. Scalable. Experience-Led.
At The Phoenix Mills Limited (PML), our business model blends long-term vision 
with operational excellence. We develop and operate high-quality, experience-led 
destinations across retail, office, hospitality, and residential formats — each designed to 
be the flagship development in its city.
Our platform is fully integrated, spanning land acquisition, master planning, design, 
development, leasing, operations, and ongoing densification of existing landmark assets. 
Strategic partnerships with global and domestic brands, institutional investors, and 
delivery experts enhance both scale and execution strength.

long-term alignment with tenants, guests, and investors.

Prudent Management: Optimising 
Operational Efficiency
Our focus on cost management and operational 
efficiency strengthened our foundation in FY2025. 
Strong cost control strategies translated into 
a consolidated EBITDA margin of 57%, a 2 
percentage-point improvement over FY2024; 
despite business expansion and increased marketing 
investments.  Cost optimisation and efficiency gains, 
preserved flexibility to undertake new projects, carry 
out asset enhancements, and explore new markets 
without overextending resources.
We also strengthened financial resilience through 
proactive debt optimisation. The average cost 
of debt reduced to 8.5% in FY2025, compared 
to 9.2% in FY2020, reflecting focused efforts on 
lowering borrowing costs. Our strategy remains 
conservative: borrowing only as projects near 
completion and refinancing them through Lease 
Rental Discounting (LRD) once operational.Our disciplined approach to cost and debt 
management enables us to expand strategically, 
while sustaining industry-leading margins and 
financial flexibility.

Capital Structure: Balance Sheet 
Resilience and Cash Flows
PML ’s balance sheet continues to exemplify 
resilience and prudence, anchoring both stability 
and future growth. As of March 2025, gross debt 
stood at ~` 4,409 crore, marginally higher year-on-
year, yet well below pre-COVID levels, despite a 
substantial capital outlay. Nearly 99% of borrowings 
as of March-2025 were secured against annuity 
income from operational assets, underscoring the 
visibility and stability of cash flows
Net debt rose to ` 2,707 crore (from ` 2,157 crore in 
March 2024), reflecting the deployment of liquidity 
for expansion rather than increased leverage. 
The net debt-to-EBITDA ratio held steady at a 
conservative ~1.2x, among the strongest in the 
sector, leaving significant headroom to fund future 
growth.
Cash generation remained a core strength. 
Operating free cash flows (after working capital 
changes, taxes, and interest paid) stood at ` 1,738 
crore. Within our core businesses, operating free 
cash flows rose 24% year-on-year to ` 1,652 crore. 
By relying primarily on these internal accruals, PML advanced expansion while keeping external 
borrowings in check.
The equity base was further reinforced during the 
year. Consolidated reserves rose to ` 10,377 crore, 
while share capital doubled to ` 72 crore following 
a 1:1 bonus issue. Together, strong reserves, 
disciplined leverage, and consistent free cash flow 
generation provide a capital structure that balances 
prudence with growth readiness.

Brand Strength 
Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai
PML ’s brand strength is rooted in three elements: consistent delivery, 
curatorial credibility, and cultural relevance. We are not only India’s leading 
developer of retail-led mixed-use assets – we are also the partner of choice 
for international brands seeking to enter or scale in India. First-to-market 
launches affirm our role as the launchpad for global retail in the country. This 
is also confirmed by the fact that ~67% of our retail space is occupied by 
nearly 178 brands present in more than 6 of our malls across India. 
Our brand relationships go beyond tenancy. We co-curate environments 
that help brands thrive – through merchandising support, cross-brand 
adjacencies, and engagement programming that drives traffic. Our properties 
serve as platforms for flagship statements, blending lifestyle, luxury, and 
location in a format that delivers consistent value to brands.
Meanwhile, our proprietary festivals – Phoenix Shopping Festival, Phoenix 
Food Festival, Phoenix Wedding Festival – and event IPs like Pink Friday act 
as both footfall drivers and brand amplifiers. These formats are iterative, 
scalable, and designed to embed our malls into the cultural fabric of the city. 
The result is that more consumers engage, more brands want to anchor, and 
more events reinforce the identity of our spaces.Skilled Workforce

A Philosophy of Inclusive Growth
At PML, our approach to social responsibility is 
built on enduring partnerships that create shared 
value. During FY2025, we channelled our CSR 
efforts into four priority areas—water security, 
education, healthcare, and dignity for vulnerable 
communities—ensuring that growth translates into 
real progress for society. These initiatives touched 
thousands of lives directly, and millions more 
indirectly through systemic improvements in water, 
livelihoods, and education.
Water Security as a Foundation of 
Prosperity
For over two decades, PML has collaborated with 
Aakar Charitable Trust (ACT) to combat water 
scarcity in some of India’s most drought-prone 
regions. This partnership demonstrates how 
sustained efforts can regenerate communities, 
strengthen livelihoods, and create lasting prosperity.~`25  crore
Allocated towards CSR activities in FY2025 (group level)
Allocated across water 
conservation, education, health, 
and rehabilitation in FY2025
By March 2025, ACT had facilitated the construction of 
801 check dams and 397 ponds across 11 Indian states — 
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, 
Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, 
and Chhattisgarh. These interventions have improved 
water access for over 1,196 villages, directly benefitting 
1.8 million people. The results go beyond water: with food 
security restored and multiple cropping seasons enabled, 
annual earnings in these villages have risen significantly, 
underscoring the multiplier effect of water security.Our Capitals à  Social & Relationship Capital

The Phoenix Mills LimitedA Collaborative Model for Change
ACT’s approach is rooted in community ownership 
and behavioural transformation:
 Engagement & Awareness – ACT volunteers 
begin by earning the trust of villagers, raising 
awareness of water harvesting, and setting 
conditions for social reform (discouraging 
practices such as child marriage, dowry, and 
substance abuse).
 Joint Contribution – Villages contribute 30% of 
costs, while ACT contributes 70%, creating a 
sense of ownership and sustainability.
 Rigorous Planning – Each site undergoes 
feasibility, economic, social, and environmental 
impact studies before implementation.
 Quality Construction – Structures are 
designed by experts with experience, ensuring 
transparency, durability, and cost-effectiveness.
 Transformative Impact – Once completed, 
check dams fill during monsoons, enabling 
bountiful harvests, higher incomes, and  
drought-free villages.
Our collaboration with ACT is about philanthropy and empowerment. By securing water, we help villages secure their futures.Education and Skills: Breaking Cycles 
of Inequality
Education is the most powerful lever of social 
transformation. Through partnerships with 
organisations such as Gram Mangal, Light of Life 
Trust, and Friends of Tribals, to name a few, our 
efforts are designed to widen access and improve 
the quality and continuity of learning.
Friends of Tribals Society (FTS): Through its Ekal 
Vidyalaya “one-teacher school” model, FTS provides 
values-based education across 18 states, reaching 
deep into tribal and rural areas.
Light of Life Trust: Its Project Anando supports 
secondary school students with academic coaching, 
life skills, and livelihood training, ensuring continuity 
in education.
Gram Mangal: This Maharashtra-based initiative 
builds joyful, culturally rooted learning environments, 
with teacher training that has become a benchmark 
for inclusive pedagogy.

External Traffic Management 
At Phoenix Palladium, we initiated an External Traffic 
Management (ETM) programme to ease congestion 
in one of India’s busiest metros. A dedicated 
team of 15 wardens, led by an ex-Mumbai Police 
supervisor, was deployed within a 2–3 km radius of 
the mall. Their efforts streamlined access, improved 
pedestrian safety, and made customer journeys 
smoother. Joint operations with the Brihanmumbai 
Municipal Corporation (BMC) and Mumbai Police 
led to the removal of unauthorised bikes, debris,  
and hawkers. A U-turn provision at Senapati Bapat 
Marg further decongested the flow, setting a 
benchmark for private–public coordination in  
traffic management.

Energy Management
Our destinations operate seven days a week, with 
intensive cooling, lighting, and diverse tenant usage. 
The scale and operational intensity of our assets 
make energy management a critical part of PML ’s 
environmental footprint. In FY2025, total electricity 
consumption across our operational assets (retail, 
offices, hotels) stood at 297 GwH, an increase from 
266 GwH in FY2024. This growth reflects the ramp-
up of our newly launched retail destinations.
Phoenix Mall of the Millennium in Pune (opened 
in September 2023) and Phoenix Mall of Asia in 
Bengaluru (opened in October 2023) were operational 
for the full year for the first time in FY2025, while 
Palladium Ahmedabad (opened in February 2023) also 
continued to scale up. Average trading occupancies 
for these destinations also improved significantly, from 
60% for FY2024 to 85% for FY2025. These gains 
underline both the strong traction of our new assets 
and the corresponding impact on energy usage.
We continue to invest in energy-efficiency 
technologies across assets:
 LED retrofits to replace legacy lighting systems.
 Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) on chillers 
and air-handling units (AHUs), reducing energy 
consumption compared to fixed-speed systems.
 Advanced Building Management Systems (BMS) 
enable real-time monitoring and optimisation of 
loads, lighting, and HVAC. 
 MERV 13 air filters and high-efficiency cooling 
systems ensure energy savings while improving 
indoor air quality.
 EV charging stations, with over 100 installed 
across 6 centers in the portfolio and more  
under planning.
These measures have helped stabilisation of energy 
consumption curves at established malls, even as 
footfalls increase. Energy use is also influenced by 
seasonal demand cycles and geographic conditions 
across our portfolio, factors that make operational 
efficiency and technology adoption even more 
important.
Looking ahead, PML will continue working 
to moderate the growth of absolute energy 
consumption as the portfolio expands, while 
progressively substituting fossil-based power with 
renewable energy.Ramp-up at new malls increased energy use in 
FY2025, but efficiency measures at established 
assets kept consumption growth in check.
Steadily scaling renewables energy use 
across assets, strengthening both climate 
impact and operational resilience.
Renewable Energy Transition
Renewable energy is at the heart of PML ’s 
decarbonisation journey. In FY2025, renewables met 
34% of the energy requirements of Common Area 
and HVAC across the retail portfolio. Renewable 
energy consumption has more than doubled over 
the last five years, rising from ~27 million units in 
FY2021, to 41 million units in FY2023 and now, in 
FY2025, close to 58 million units. This progress 
reflects deliberate investments in renewable energy 
(both long-term and short-term contracts) to balance 
supply and demand. Rooftop solar also contributes, 
with ~590 kW of panels installed across assets. 
The impact is tangible. In FY2025 alone, renewable 
energy procurement enabled us to avoid 
approximately 22,800 tonnes of CO2 equivalent 
emissions, equivalent to the carbon absorbed by 
377,000 tree seedlings grown for a decade.* These 
equivalencies underscore how renewable energy 
is a powerful narrative of climate-positive action. 
Expanding the share of renewable energy also 
strengthens operational resilience, shields against 
grid price volatility, and builds brand equity with 
environmentally conscious tenants, partners,  
and consumers.
PML has long-term aspiration for over 70% of energy 
requirements to be met through renewable sources. 
We continue to work towards:
1. Scaling Power Purchase Agreements 
(PPAs): Partnering with established renewable 
developers for steady supply. In FY2025, we 
signed new agreements for Phoenix Mall of the 
Millennium, Pune, and The St. Regis, Mumbai, 
with further opportunities under evaluation 
in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and 
Madhya Pradesh.
2. Onsite Solar Expansion: Rooftop and façade-
mounted solar PV systems are being designed 
into new assets where architectural  
feasibility allows. 
3. Portfolio-Wide Integration: Established assets 
such as Phoenix MarketCity Mumbai, Pune, 
Bangalore, and Phoenix Palassio, Lucknow 
are already running on significant shares of 
renewable power, demonstrating integration 
across the portfolio. 
The renewable energy transition is embedded in 
PML ’s capital allocation and operational planning. 
Every additional unit of green energy strengthens our 
brand equity with environmentally conscious retail 
partners, investors and increasingly  
discerning consumers.
*Estimates based on Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator 
of U.S. Environmental Protection Agency

Compost generated from wet waste in FY2025 and 
reused in landscapingWater management is a vital part of PML ’s natural 
capital strategy. Our assets, concentrated in urban 
areas, are inherently water-intensive, with large 
restroom facilities, cooling systems, F&B operations, 
and landscaping requirements. We recognise that 
urban water supply cannot be taken for granted, 
and are committed to managing it responsibly 
through efficient use, recycling and reuse. 
In FY2025, total water consumption across the 
portfolio was 31 lakh KL, compared with 29 lakh KL 
in FY2024. Similar to energy usage, this increase is 
a function of the ramp-up of new assets and higher 
trading occupancies. As these destinations stabilise, 
their built-in efficiency systems are expected to 
deliver stronger outcomes over time.Every drop reused strengthens resilience: 
conserving water, cutting costs, and 
ensuring uninterrupted operations.
Every stream managed responsibly: 
from recycling to composting to plastics 
reduction, turning waste into value.
PML continues to invest in multiple layers of water 
conservation:
 Smart fixtures: such as sensors, aerators, and 
waterless urinals reducing wastage significantly 
compared to conventional fittings. 
 Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs): are installed 
across our assets, with capacities calibrated 
to local demand. These plants enable reuse of 
treated water for toilet flushing, HVAC cooling 
towers, and landscaping. 
 Rainwater harvesting systems: that capture 
rooftop runoff for reuse and channels non-
rooftop runoff into recharge pits, conserving 
potable water and replenishing aquifers
 Groundwater discharge reuse: natural 
groundwater inflows at certain locations are 
captured, treated, and channelled for domestic 
or cooling purposes, reducing fresh draw.
Illustrative Outcomes of our strategy:
 STP upgrades and optimisation across malls 
have saved over 94,000 KL of water annually, 
translating to nearly ` 1.13 crore in annual 
savings.
 Smart fixtures at Phoenix Citadel, Phoenix Mall 
of Asia, and Phoenix Mall of the Millennium, 
delivered an additional ~ `2.5 crore in savings.
While overall water consumption rose due to 
portfolio expansion, the share of recycled and 
non-potable water continues to increase. This is 
particularly critical in water-stressed cities, where 
long-term water security ensures uninterrupted 
tenant operations and reduced reliance on 
municipal sources.
For PML, water stewardship is not a compliance 
tick-box but a driver of resilience and efficiency: 
ensuring continuity of operations while delivering 
measurable business value.

INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25As high-footfall destinations, our assets generate 
large volumes of waste each day, from food, 
packaging, to operational dry waste. Managing 
this responsibly is central to our commitment to 
reducing environmental impact and building  
circular systems.
In FY2025, total waste rose to 52 lakh kg, vs 43 lakh 
kg in FY2024, reflecting higher footfalls and ramp 
up at new assets. Importantly, this growth in waste 
volumes has been matched with stronger waste 
management measures, keeping environmental 
impact in check.
Our approach includes: 
 Segregation & Recycling: through partnerships 
with certified third-party recyclers. By 
institutionalising vendor tie-ups, PML ensures 
compliance with CPCB/MPCB guidelines. Turning waste into value: Organic Waste 
Converters transform wet waste into nutrient-rich 
compost, reused in landscaping and reducing 
dependence on chemical fertilisers.
 Safe Disposal of Hazardous Streams: Hazardous 
waste, including oils, paints are handled exclusively 
through authorised  
vendors, ensuring adherence to national disposal 
standards.
 Responsible E-Waste Handling:  Tie-ups with 
licensed recyclers in place to handle electronic 
waste streams responsibly as operations become 
increasingly technology-enabled.
Waste management also enhances the quality 
of experience within our destinations. Cleaner 
environments, reduced odours, and visible recycling 
loops ensure comfort for customers while embedding 
sustainability as a lived and seen practice.

rigorous benchmarks of sustainability, efficiency, and well-being. These certifications validate choices in 
architecture, engineering, and materials while strengthening competitiveness with tenants, customers,  
and investors.

Design Interventions Behind Certification
Certifications are the outcome of a deeper design philosophy. From the outset, PML integrates 
sustainability features into every development: energy-efficient HVAC and lighting, water-saving fixtures 
and treatment systems, advanced waste management, and use of locally sourced green materials. Design 
also emphasises high-performance glazed façades, landscaped open spaces etc. that enhance both 
efficiency and wellbeing. Together, these choices deliver measurable business value: lowering operating 
costs, extending asset lifespans, and creating healthier environments that support tenant productivity and 
customer experience.

INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25Emissions & Climate Reporting
In FY2025, Scope 1 and 2 emissions from common 
area operations at Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai, 
amounted to 2,428 tCO2e. This provides useful 
insights into operational energy-related emissions 
and informs our approach to expanding coverage 
across other assets over time.
Our GHG reduction approach is integrated into 
the broader natural capital strategy: scaling 
renewable energy, driving efficiency at mature 
assets, and embedding low-carbon design 
in new developments. In the past, we have 
also undertaken focused studies, including a 
decarbonisation roadmap at Project Rise, Mumbai 
and a sustainability study at Phoenix MarketCity 
Bangalore. The insights from these projects can  
be extended across other assets, helping us  
shape a portfolio-wide approach as reporting  
and strategy evolve.
As measurement expands, we also intend to 
progressively include tenant energy use, embodied 
carbon in new developments, and other indirect 
sources. We are evaluating global frameworks such 
as SBTi and TCFD to guide the evolution of our 
disclosures
Climate Risk and Resilience
Climate risks such as flooding, extreme rainfall, 
and rising temperatures have direct implications for 
PML ’s operations. We are responding by embedding 
resilience into design and operations: from flood 
assessments and elevated plinths in sensitive zones 
across select assets to EV charging hubs and 
renewable integration that future-proof our assets.
As our portfolio expands, these early measures 
will be scaled and deepened, positioning PML ’s 
destinations as climate-adaptive urban ecosystems 
that can withstand environmental shocks while 
ensuring continuity of operations.
Governance 
Sustainability at PML is guided from the top and 
embedded across daily operations. At the Board 
level, a dedicated Sustainability Committee, chaired 
by an Independent Director and comprising two 
Executive Directors, provides strategic oversight, 
monitors progress, and steers long-term  
ESG commitments.At the operational level, ESG responsibilities are 
integrated across functions. Operations teams 
drive initiatives on energy efficiency, renewable 
procurement, water and waste management, and 
green design, ensuring that sustainability principles 
are translated into measurable action on the ground.

Economic & Market 
Environment
Global Macroeconomic 
Overview
The global economy grew by 3.3% in 
2024 (IMF), showing resilience despite a 
period of disruptions. Growth has lacked 
strong momentum, and concerns of a 
slowdown are emerging as governments 
realign their policy priorities to address 
evolving global challenges. Trade 
tensions and policy uncertainty are 
expected to weigh on global economic 
activity in 2025. The outlook for 2025 
is marked by cautious optimism amid 
persistent uncertainties. Reflecting this, 
the IMF now projects growth of 2.8% in 
2025 and 3.0% in 2026, revised down 
from its earlier forecast of 3.3% for  
both years.  The global trade outlook has also weakened. The World Trade 
Organisation (WTO) expects global merchandise trade volumes 
to drop marginally by 0.2% in 2025, before recovering by 2.5% in 
2026. Trade flows remain under strain due to persistent inflationary 
pressures, tighter monetary policies, and heightened geopolitical 
tensions in the near term. Sluggish demand, particularly in advanced 
economies, and supply chain adjustments in response to global risks 
are likely to dampen trade flows and weigh on worldwide growth and 
investment sentiment across sectors.A notable divergence is emerging between advanced and 
emerging markets. Growth in advanced economies is expected 
to moderate to 1.4% in 2025, with the United States projected 
to grow at 1.8%. In contrast, emerging markets and developing 
economies are expected to demonstrate greater resilience, 
with growth projected at 3.7% in 2025 and 3.9% in 2026. 
India is poised to be a standout performer within this group, 
leading global growth on the back of strong domestic demand, 
structural reforms, and stable macroeconomic fundamentals. 
This divergence highlights the shifting dynamics of global growth, 
with emerging markets, particularly India, playing an increasingly 
pivotal role in sustaining global economic momentum.
A key positive has been the easing of global inflation. Headline 
inflation is now expected to decline, though at a slightly slower 
pace than forecast in January. It is projected to ease to 4.3% 
in 2025 and further to 3.6% in 2026. Within this, estimates for 
advanced economies have been revised upwards, while those 
for emerging and developing markets have been slightly adjusted 
downward for 2025. 
While global headwinds persist, the resilience of emerging markets 
provides a critical buffer. India’s strong domestic fundamentals 
position it not only as a growth outlier but also as a stabilising 
force in global economic momentum, creating a supportive 
backdrop for retail, real estate, and hospitality growth.Emerging markets and developing 
economies are expected to grow at 3.7% in 
2025, ahead of advanced economies, with a 
1.4% growth forecast for 2025.

The Phoenix Mills LimitedIndian Economic Outlook
As global trade faces a potential slowdown, 
emerging economies like India and Brazil are 
poised to benefit from the shifting of export flows 
away from traditional centres such as China. 
India, in particular, enjoys a strategic advantage: 
a strong domestic demand base and relatively 
low reliance on merchandise exports, shielding it 
from the immediate impacts of rising tariffs. India’s 
services-led export portfolio adds resilience amid 
evolving trade patterns. The IMF projects India’s GDP growth at 6.2% 
for 2025 and 6.3% for 2026, well above the 
global average and emerging market peers. 
Robust domestic demand, continued reforms, 
and sustained infrastructure investment and 
development support this outlook. India’s lower 
reliance on merchandise exports and its active 
services sector contribute to stability during global 
trade interruptions. With sound macroeconomic 
fundamentals and steady policy support, India is 
expected to be a major driver of global economic 
growth over the medium term. 
In light of emerging headwinds and signs of a 
potential moderating growth momentum, the 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) revised its GDP growth 
forecast for 2025–26 downward by 20 basis 
points to 6.5%, compared to its earlier projection 
in February. To support economic activity and 
ease financing conditions, the RBI has undertaken 
a series of rate cuts this year, most recently in 
June 2025, when the Monetary Policy Committee 
reduced the repo rate by 50 basis points to 5.5%. 
This cumulative easing of 100 basis points since 
February signals a shift in policy stance towards 
supporting growth over inflation amidst a complex 
global environment.

Global Consumer Sentiments
According to Ipsos, the Global Consumer Confidence Index slipped by 0.4 points 
in April 2025 from the previous month, reflecting rising concerns over inflation, 
trade tensions, and broader economic uncertainty. Confidence levels fell sharply in 
advanced economies such as the United States and parts of Europe, while emerging 
markets remained relatively stable. Consumers expressed increasing caution 
regarding their financial outlook, contributing to more restrained spending behaviour 
across major sectors.
Confidence levels dropped sharply 
across advanced economies, while 
emerging markets maintained  
relative stability.
Euromonitor International’s “Top Global Consumer 
Trends 2025” highlights how consumers navigate 
this environment. Key emerging behaviours 
include strongly emphasising “Wiser Wallets”: 
where strategic, researched spending replaces 
impulse buying and a marked preference for 
brands offering credible, tangible value. At the 
same time, health, wellness, and sustainability 
remain powerful drivers of purchasing decisions 
with growing demand for preventative healthcare 
and eco-conscious and cost-effective products. 
Moreover, with increasing information overload, 
the “Filtered Focus” trend underscores the 
demand for clear communication, simplified 
experiences, and trusted interactions. 
According to Deloitte’s Global State of the 
Consumer Tracker, while consumers in several 
advanced economies displayed resilience, 
there was growing caution around discretionary 
spending, particularly in travel, dining, and luxury 
goods. A notable trend was the “flight to value,” 
with consumers prioritising essentials and re-
evaluating spending habits amid rising living costs.
Indian Consumption Landscape
India’s consumer market is undergoing a 
significant transformation, positioning itself as one 
of the most dynamic and sought-after markets 
globally. According to a report by Morgan Stanley, 
India is set to become the world’s third-largest 
economy and the most attractive consumer 
market over the next decade, driven by a rising 
affluent middle class, favourable demographics, 
and accelerating urbanisation. Rising disposable 
incomes and a shift in spending patterns towards 
discretionary and premium categories are 
expected to reshape the consumption narrative.
According to a report by Edelweiss Mutual Fund, 
India’s consumer market is expected to become 
the world’s second-largest by 2030, surpassing 
Japan and Germany. Consumer spending in India 
is projected to rise sharply from USD 2.4 trillion 
in 2024 to USD 4.3 trillion by 2030, reflecting the 
country’s strong economic fundamentals, rising 
household incomes, and rapid urbanisation. Key 
sectors such as retail, healthcare, education, and 
financial services are set to benefit significantly 
from this surge. Furthermore, the continued 
expansion of organised retail, increasing internet 
penetration, and the growing influence of digital 
platforms are expected to accelerate the evolution 
of consumer spending patterns further. Consumer confidence in India remains resilient 
despite global headwinds, with private consumption 
expenditure on an upward trend, suggesting 
sustained consumer confidence and healthy 
demand. Strong government spending and robust 
performance across sectors such as construction, 
financial services, and trade are reinforcing this 
demand. Significantly, easing inflation has further 
strengthened household purchasing power. Notably, 
according to official MOSPI data, India’s headline 
CPI inflation stood at 3.6% in February 2025, eased 
to 2.1% in June, and declined further to 1.2% in 
July: its lowest level in over eight years. This sharp 
decline, mainly driven by food prices, has provided 
additional tailwinds to consumption activity and 
underscores the durability of India’s demand story.
India’s consumer spending is set to 
almost double to USD 4.3 trillion by 2030, 
according to Edelweiss Mutual Fund.

India’s commercial office sector showed strong

According to CBRE 2025 India Market Outlook 
Report, leveraging on India’s extensive talent pool, 
global firms are increasingly positioning their GCCs 
as strategic hubs / second headquarters, driving

of high-value capabilities. As per the report, in

of the total office space absorption across top cities.Grade A office spaces in Bengaluru, Hyderabad,

interest, supported by a growing preference for 
premium, flexible, and tech-enabled workspaces. 
According to CBRE 2025 India Market Outlook 
Report, on the supply side, 60–65% of new 
developments in 2025 are anticipated to be located 
within integrated tech parks in key cities, including 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, 
Chennai, and Pune. Developers are increasingly 
focused on delivering investment-grade, green-
certified, and amenities-rich office spaces that align 
with occupiers’ evolving sustainability and employee 
well-being goals.
Leasing momentum is expected to remain steady 
as occupiers expand beyond traditional hubs into 
emerging gateway and Tier II cities, seeking talent 
and strategic diversification. According to CBRE 
2025 India Market Outlook Report, approximately 
54% of office leasing in 2022-24 was in green-

yet resilient, particularly across prime micro-

community-building amenities, and flexible layouts, 
reinforcing the hospitality-led, experience-driven 
evolution of India’s commercial office landscape.Retail Real Estate in India
India’s retail real estate sector showed resilience 
and transformation through 2024, navigating 
macroeconomic headwinds and evolving consumer 
behaviours. The industry benefits from strong 
economic growth, rising disposable incomes, 
a young demographic profile, and a clear shift 
towards premiumisation and experiential retailing. 
According to ANAROCK’s Indian Retail: Changing 
Orbits for a New Trajectory report, India’s retail 
market is projected to expand from USD 1.2 trillion 
in 2023 to USD 2.5 trillion by 2035, a steady 
CAGR of 6%. Organised retail is set to rise from a 
12% share in 2023 to 17–19% by 2035, offering 
significant headroom for modern retail formats to 
flourish. 
Demand dynamics remained robust across top-
tier cities and are increasingly penetrating Tier II 
and III markets. According to CBRE 2025 India 
Market Outlook, driven by continued expansionary 
sentiments of numerous global and domestic 
brands, retail leasing activity in India’s Tier 1 cities 
touched ~6.4 million sq. ft. in 2024.  
Supply, however, remained constrained during 
2024, reducing vacancy levels. Vacancy rates in 
prime investment-grade malls have significantly 
declined, from 15.4% in 2019 to around 7.8% 
by 2024, underlining healthy space absorption. 
(ANAROCK Retail RELEAP Report 2024). 
Developers respond by prioritising superior mall 
developments, strongly focusing on sustainability, 
wellness amenities, and digital integration. Cushman 
& Wakefield’s report highlights that superior Grade 
A+ malls (about 39 million sq. ft. across top cities) 
are witnessing 3–4% vacancy rates and have 
recorded a 29% rental growth since 2019. 
A clear trend of premiumisation is reshaping India’s 
retail landscape. Shoppers are shifting towards 
aspirational and discretionary categories, moving 
beyond essentials. Beauty & Wellness and F&B 
categories have expanded their share in mall 
leasing to 15–18% from 6–8% pre-COVID, while 
athleisure and sportswear brands have increased 
their footprint, reflecting evolving consumer 
lifestyles. Responding to these shifts, developers are 
reimagining retail spaces as lifestyle hubs offering 
a curated blend of retail, entertainment, dining, and 
community experiences. Beyond Tier I cities, Tier 
II and III locations such as Indore, Ahmedabad, 
Lucknow, Jaipur, and Coimbatore are emerging as 
major retail growth centres. Vacancy rates in prime malls dropped 
sharply from 15.4% in 2019 to 8.1% in 
2024, reflecting strong absorption.
60–65% of new developments are 
expected in integrated tech parks across 
major Indian cities.
Looking ahead, India’s retail real estate sector 
is positioned for sustained growth, fuelled by 
demographic tailwinds, rising affluence, increasing 
brand consciousness, and the ongoing evolution of 
retail spaces into experience-driven destinations. 
Developers and brands that strategically align with 
these changing preferences, through premium 
spaces, ESG compliance, and hybrid physical-
digital strategies, will be best placed to capture 
future opportunities.

Hospitality Sector in India
India’s hospitality sector is experiencing an 
unprecedented boom, marked by substantial 
investment activity and rapid expansion plans. 
According to JLL, the industry is poised to add 
approximately 42,000 new hotel keys over the next 
five years, reflecting the largest growth pipeline 
seen in recent times. This surge is driven by robust 
domestic demand, a rebound in business and 
leisure travel, and increasing interest from global 
hotel chains seeking to expand their footprint 
in India. Major cities like Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, 
Bengaluru, and Hyderabad continue to lead 
development. Tier II and III cities are emerging as 
essential growth hubs, supported by improving 
infrastructure, rising disposable incomes, and 
evolving travel patterns. 
The outlook remains positive, with ICRA projecting 
11–13% YoY growth in FY2025, supported by 
strong domestic leisure travel, increased demand 
from MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and 
Exhibitions), and steady business travel. Even during 
the temporary lull caused by general elections, 
demand remained resilient, setting the stage for 
future growth.New supply has been measured, with the premium 
room inventory across 12 key cities projected to 
grow at a CAGR of ~4.5–5.0% between FY2023 
and FY2026, ensuring that demand will continue 
to outpace supply. This disciplined approach is 
expected to prevent oversupply issues and facilitate 
a prolonged upcycle in the industry. The pan-India 
premium hotel occupancy rate is estimated to be 
around 70–72% for FY2025 and is likely to improve 
further to 72–74% in FY2026.
Revenue and profitability metrics have also improved 
significantly. Average room rates (ARRs) for premium 
hotels are estimated at INR 8,000–8,200 for FY2025, 
with a further rise projected to INR 8,200–8,500 in 
FY2026. RevPAR (Revenue per Available Room) 
has almost reached pre-2008 peak levels and is 
anticipated to rise to INR 5,900–6,300 in FY2026. 
Operating margins of large hotel players are expected 
to be around 34–36% for FY2025 and FY2026, up 
from pre-COVID averages of 20–22%, driven by cost 
rationalisation and operating leverage.
Higher business accruals have also strengthened 
the sector’s capital structures, improving debt 
coverage metrics. With sustained momentum from 
domestic tourism, the rise of spiritual tourism, and 
the continued growth of Tier II city demand, India’s 
hospitality sector is expected to maintain its firm 
footing well into FY2026. Company Overview

Retail 
PML ’s retail portfolio today spans 12 iconic, 
experience-driven city centre destinations totalling 
nearly 11.5 million sq. ft. across 8 major cities in 
India. This includes marquee assets such as Phoenix 
Palladium (Mumbai), Phoenix MarketCity (Mumbai, 
Pune, Bengaluru, and Chennai), Phoenix Palassio 
(Lucknow), Phoenix Citadel (Indore), Palladium 
Ahmedabad, Phoenix Mall of the Millennium (Pune) 
and Phoenix Mall of Asia (Bengaluru). 
Our retail assets are recognised for their scale, 
prime city-centre locations, and immersive 
experiences that consistently deliver results. With 
consistently high trading occupancy, sustained 
consumption growth, and resilient rental income, 
our portfolio has become a benchmark for 
destination retail in India. Each mall combines 
premium positioning with a carefully curated brand 
mix, balancing global and Indian labels with diverse 
dining, entertainment, and community-centric 
offerings to drive long-term footfall and tenant 
productivity.
As consumer expectations evolve, our destinations 
are continually refreshed and repositioned to remain 
aspirational and relevant. By creating destinations 
where retail, leisure, and dining converge, we 
continue to deliver environments that engage, 
inspire, and drive sustained consumption.
Expansions and Pipeline
In November 2024, PML unveiled the West Zone at 
Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai, adding ~250,000 sq. ft. 
of retail space to our flagship asset. This expansion 
deepened our presence in South Mumbai’s premium 
catchment and delivered immediate traction, with 
~14 stores opened during FY2025. The zone 
features high-impact anchors such as the largest 
Uniqlo store in South Mumbai, Lifestyle, and flagship 
outlets from brands like Nykaa Luxe, Tira, GAP , 
Levi’s, Celio, Navyasa, and House of Masaba. A 
defining highlight was the India debut of Bershka, 
which marked the brand’s entry into the country. 
To further elevate the experience, in July 2025, 
we launched Gourmet Village: a two-level curated 
dining and entertainment area in the West Zone. Of 
the 25 planned outlets in this space, 12 are already 
operational, including Game Palacio, a dynamic 
dining and recreation zone. Looking ahead, the West 
Zone will be enhanced with active leisure avenues 
such as pickleball and paddle courts, aligning 
with evolving lifestyle preferences and reinforcing 
Phoenix Palladium’s position as Mumbai’s premier 
destination for retail, dining, and leisure.
Retail Project Pipeline:
PML is on track to expand its national retail footprint 
from 12 operating malls across 8 cities today to 17 
malls across 13 cities by 2030. This next phase of 
growth will be driven by a mix of new asset launches 
and densification of existing assets, enabling us to 
both deepen our presence in existing markets and 
foray into high-potential new markets. 
We are currently developing retail destinations in 
Kolkata, Surat, and Coimbatore, along with retail-
led mixed-use developments in Thane and the 
Chandigarh Metropolitan Region (CMR). These 
projects will add considerable scale and regional 
diversity to our portfolio. Simultaneously, we are 
expanding some of our assets: Phoenix Palladium, 
Mumbai, Phoenix MarketCity Mumbai and Phoenix 
MarketCity Bangalore to enhance both scale and 
consumer experience.~250,000 sq. ft of premium retail space

at Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai in 
November 2024.
Collectively, these initiatives are expected to add ~7 million sq. ft. of operational retail space, taking our 
Gross Leasable Area (GLA) from ~11.5 msft today to over 18 msft by 2030.

Elevating Everyday Experiences

Financial & Operational Performance
Income from Operations
In FY2025 we delivered a strong performance 
across our core businesses of retail, commercial 
offices, and hospitality. These verticals collectively 
delivered revenue of ` 3,507 crore, reflecting a 
16% year-on-year growth, and an EBITDA of 
`2,111 crore, underscoring the continued strength 
and cash-generating capability of our annuity-led 
business model.  Residential sales moderated 
compared to the previous year and as a result, 
consolidated revenue from operations was down 4% 
year-on-year to ` 3,814 crore.
From a standalone perspective, which comprises 
operations of Phoenix Palladium Mumbai (including 
commercial offices – Phoenix House, located in 
the same complex), revenue from operations stood 
at `486 crore in FY2025, reflecting a 4% change 
compared to ` 466 crore in FY2024.
Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, 
Depreciation, and Amortisation 
(EBITDA)
The consolidated EBITDA stood steady at ` 2,161 
crore in FY2025, as compared to ` 2,177 crore 
achieved in FY2024. Consolidated EBITDA margins 
improved by 200 basis points to 57%, compared to 
a margin of 55% recorded in FY2024.
On a standalone basis, FY2025 EBITDA stood at 
`300 crore, compared to ` 312 crore in FY2024, 
reflecting a 4% decline. EBITDA margins on a 
standalone basis moderated by 500 bps now 
standing at 62%, compared to 67% in FY2024.
Interest and Depreciation
Standalone depreciation and amortisation stood 
at `45 crore in FY2025, compared to ` 35 crore in 
FY2024, reflecting a growth of 28%.On a consolidated basis, depreciation and 
amortisation increased to ` 327 crore in FY2025, 
against `270 crore recorded in FY2024, registering 
a 21% growth. This increase is attributed to the 
expansion of the operational portfolio, including the 
launch of new assets during the year.
Standalone borrowings stood at ` 749 crore as of 
FY2025, compared to ` 720 crore as of FY2024. 
Interest expense on a standalone basis was ` 73 
crore for FY2025, compared to ` 65 crore in 
FY2024, showing a 13% change.
On the consolidated front, borrowings stood at 
`4,663 crore in FY2025, up marginally from ` 4,612 
crore in FY2024. Finance Cost increased to ` 403 crore in FY2025, compared to ` 396 crore in 
FY2024, primarily driven by additional debt raised 
during the year. Blended average cost of debt was 
at 8.50% as of March 2025, compared to 8.81% as 
of March 2024. 
Profit After Tax and Minority Interest
Standalone Profit After Tax stood at ` 337 crore 
in FY2025, compared to ` 280 crore recorded in 
FY2024, reflecting a 20% growth.
Consolidated Profit After Tax, Share in Associates 
and Minority Interest for FY2025 stood at ` 984 crore, 
compared to ` 1,099 crore achieved in FY2024.
Balance Sheet
Share Capital
In FY2025, our share capital doubled to ` 72 crore 
from `36 crore in FY2024, primarily on account of 
the 1:1 bonus issue undertaken during the year. 
Standalone reserves and surplus rose to ` 5,245 
crore in FY2025 from ` 5,023 crore in the previous 
year, while consolidated reserves and surplus 
increased to ` 10,377 crore from ` 9,422 crore  
in FY2024.
Non-Current and Current Liabilities
Standalone long term borrowings increased to 
`682 crore in FY2025, compared to ` 617 crore in 
FY2024. The consolidated non-current borrowings 
rose to ` 3,847 crore in FY2025 from ` 3,813 crore 
in FY2024.We maintain strong liquidity position, with 
approximately 99% of the debt backed by annuity 
income from operational assets. Interest coverage 
ratio remained healthy at 4.9x, as against 5.2x 
recorded in FY2024.
Standalone non-current liabilities were at ` 765 crore,

Risk Management 
At PML, risk management is integral to achieving 
organisational objectives and building long-
term resilience. The Company operates under a 
structured Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) 
framework, which follows a continuous cycle of 
risk identification, assessment, prioritisation, and 
response. This framework is complemented by 
ongoing monitoring and review, ensuring that 
materialised risks are effectively controlled and 
managed. By anticipating shifts in both internal and 
external environments, PML remains agile and well-
prepared to address emerging challenges. A. Risk Identification
Risk management begins with a rigorous 
identification of detecting potential threats or 
vulnerabilities that could impact PML ’s vision or 
operations. This involves a comprehensive analysis 
of the internal and external environments in which 
we operate and the development of a detailed  
risk inventory.Risks are categorised into two broad levels:
 Enterprise-wide Risks: Strategic risks with 
a mid-to-long-term implications including 
operational risks with broader organisation-wide 
consequences such as reputational impact. 
These are addressed through the ERM policies 
and procedures.
 Operational-level Risks: Risks arising from 
day-to-day activities with short-to-medium-term 
impact. Such risks may arise from evolving 
processes, new business offerings, or routine 
operations. These are mitigated through 
internal checks and process controls, regularly 
evaluated by the Internal Audit department, as 
part of PML ’s internal assurance programme.
B. Risk Assessment
Risk assessment involves understanding the nature 
and extent of identified risks, evaluating both the 
potential impact and likelihood of occurrence to 
determine their significance. Each identified risk is 
analysed on the following parameters:
 Time to manifest: the expected timeframe for 
the risk to materialise
 Likelihood: the probability of its occurrence
 Impact: the severity of consequences if the risk 
materialises
The responsibility for conducting these assessments 
lies with the designated risk owners, who may 
consult the management for guidance. Insights from 
this process directly shape risk response strategies, 
ensuring that resources are directed towards the 
most material exposures.
C. Risk Prioritisation
Following assessment, risks are prioritised to 
determine the level of response and resource 
allocation. The goal is to highlight residual risks: 
those remaining after controls are applied, that fall 
outside PML ’s defined risk appetite.
Risk prioritisation facilitates:
 Escalation to the appropriate level of 
management
 Strategic alignment of resources
 Timely implementation of mitigation plans
While financial risk metrics guide the ranking 
process, non-financial considerations—such as media scrutiny, regulatory impact, or social 
obligations—are also factored in. Ultimately, risk 
ranking is aligned with business objectives, and all 
risks beyond the defined threshold are flagged for 
further response.
D. Risk Response
Risk response focuses on implementing actions to 
manage prioritised risks, either by strengthening 
existing controls or introducing new ones where 
needed. Each response is regularly reviewed for 
effectiveness, with clear accountability assigned to 
designated mitigation owners.
The four categories of Risk Response are:
 Avoid: Discontinuing the activity causing the risk
 Reduce: Implementing actions to decrease the 
likelihood or impact
 Share: Transferring or sharing risk (e.g., through 
insurance or partnerships)
 Accept: Acknowledging the risk without taking 
further action
This comprehensive approach ensures PML remains 
resilient, proactive, and aligned with its strategic 
objectives in an evolving business environment.
PML follows a continuous cycle 
of risk identification, assessment, 
prioritisation, and response to ensure 
organisational resilience.
